11th. December. 1918
REPORT ON Prominent Russian revolutionaries in Shanghai.
Made by D. S. Sullivan. Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.
Sir,
I beg to report that I interviewed V. Grosse Esq., Russian Consul-General, at the Russian Consulate on the morning of the 10th inst.
I showed Mr. Grosse the attached slip (marked No. 2) and newspaper cuttings. He agreed that the information contained in the typewritten paper is correct. He stated that he had read the articles in the newspapers, and considers it very unfortunate that the newspapers should give such prominence to reports of their interviews with these men, and asserts that the claims of Avksentieff and his comrades to be the champions of Liberal and Democratic opinion in Russia is rubbish.
The Consul-General stated that the four men had visited the Russian Consulate but that he had not seen them. They had however interviewed the Vice-Consul.
They have also visited the other allied Consulates and endeavoured to get their passports vised in order to proceed to Europe, but so far have not been successful.
He is unable to say whether their passports will eventually be vised or not.
Mr. Grosse states that some Russians are reporting to him the movements of these four men. So far they have only visited such places as the Carlton Cafe, picture shows, etc, and he suggests that the Police keep a watch in order to find out who visits the men at their hotel. He is most anxious to find out about the poorer class of visitors received by the refugees, but emphasizes that as there is nothing alleged against them,

由 D. S. Sullivan 撰写。由首席探长转呈。
先生，
谨此报告，本人于本月10日上午在俄国领事馆会见了俄国总领事 V. Grosse 先生。
本人向 Grosse 先生展示了附带的纸条（标记为第2号）及报纸剪报。他同意打字文件中所载信息属实。他表示已阅读报纸上的文章，并认为报纸如此突出报道对这些人的采访是非常不幸的，并断言 Avksentieff 及其同伙自称是俄国自由民主舆论捍卫者的说法纯属无稽之谈。
总领事表示，这四人曾访问俄国领事馆，但他并未接见他们。不过，他们会见了副领事。
他们还访问了其他协约国领事馆，试图为其护照签证以便前往欧洲，但迄今未获成功。
他无法说明他们的护照最终是否会获得签证。
Grosse 先生称，有些俄国人正在向他报告这四人的行踪。到目前为止，他们仅去过卡尔顿咖啡馆（Carlton Cafe）、电影院等场所，他建议警方进行监视，以查明有哪些人前往他们的旅馆拜访这些人。他非常希望能查明难民所接待的较贫困阶层的访客情况，但他强调，由于目前没有任何针对他们的指控，

THE COUP D'ETAT
OMSK.

AVKSENTIEFF AND
COMPANIONS IN SHANGHAI.

CHARGE AGAINST THEM.

By Captain George Synnerberg.

On Thursday last, December 5, there arrived in Shanghai Messrs. N. D. Avksentieff, Argunoff, Zenzinoff and Rogoffsky, former members of the Russian Provisional Government and of the directorate of five, which was displaced from power at Omsk on November 18.

These apostles of the Russian Revolution formerly enjoyed great influence and are very well known not only in Russia, but even abroad, and the most prominent of the party, Mr. Avksentieff, has successively been President of the Russian Peasants Soviet, Minister of the Interior at the time of the Bolshevik coup d'état, President of the Provisional Government at Samara, Ufa, and later on President of the Provisional Russian Government at Omsk. In such a capacity it was his duty to resist the Bolsheviks and to support the formation of a new Russian army, which was to fight against the traitors and Germans side by side with the gallant Czecho-Slovaks, British, French and Italian contingents. We shall see from the following lines, how this gentleman fulfilled his duties. As he and his companions have been arrested in Omsk and subsequently expelled from Russia, after having promised not to take any part in Russian politics, and as their intention is to go to England, perhaps it will be of interest to the English public to know exactly why they were arrested and expelled.

Evidence at Court-martial.

These four gentlemen were arrested on November 18 by some Cossack officers, who were court-martialled when they gave the following evidence, the translation being taken from all Russian papers.

The officers did not deny that they arrested the above mentioned members of the Siberian Government, but they pleaded not guilty, as the only motive which forced them to act as they did was their intense desire for the salvation of their country.

Colonel Volkov said that he saw from the very beginning in what extraordinary difficulties the new Russian statesmanship had to be reborn. The course of events convinced him that the task of regenerating the fatherland was heavily handicapped by some of the members of the directorate itself, viz. Messrs. Avksentieff, Argunoff, Zenzinoff and Rogoffsky. The latter especially was absolutely impossible from a statesmanlike point of view.

The news from the front was discouraging and it was reported that very destructive work was being conducted by the social-revolutionary party headed by V. Chernoc.

This propaganda began to produce disaffection in the ranks of the young Siberian army. Even in Omsk itself a secret Bolshevik force was organized.

Private Telegraph Wire.

The chief of the telegraph service, Captain Gleboff, gave evidence of secret conversations, which were held by direct wire with the Government at Ufa between Avksentieff and a certain Foganoffsky. Avksentieff complained that work was very difficult and that he had to contend with a "disciplined" army.

This direct wire, Captain Gleboff said, was frequently used also by Rogoffsky, Zenzinoff, Moiseenko and Brushvidt. The ribbons were always destroyed or taken home. Avksentieff used to come to the telegraph office with his own operator and insisted that the ordinary operators should not be present. The chief of the telegraphs received the information that an unknown person asked Moiseenko to send for an unknown purpose 100 million roubles from the State resources.

Colonel Zlobin, chief of the military reconnaissance bureau at General Headquarters, stated that he had obtained information of the contemplated overthrow of the present government by the social-revolutionists, who secretly formed a central committee which was said to include Messrs. Avksentieff, Chernoff, Argunoff, Vedeniapine, Volsky, Handelman, Gourevitch, Brushwid, Minor, Rogowski, Klimushkine, Fortunatoff, Fenigovsky, Lazareff and Meistracht. The party's object was to overthrow the government (which was supported by the allies) and witness said it even went so far, as to take some steps in this direction. They insisted, he said, that a detachment of about 200 men which had shown their Bolshevik sympathies, should be transferred from Novo-Nikolaevsk to Omsk. In Ufa similar Bolshevik detachments were formed under the leadership of members of the Constituent Assembly, Fortunatoff and Klimouskin. The military chief, a social revolutionist, Kalinin, was sending agitators to different military units. Ensign Springowitch was appointed chief of the military secret service department though it was proved that he had very pronounced Bolshevik sympathies.

Bolshevik Troops and Money.

Captain Affanasieff stated: the social revolutionaries had their party candidates all ready for the places as future cabinet ministers and that it was known that Avksentieff had at his disposal about 200 million roubles, which money witness averred, was sent to him to Omsk by the Bolshevik troops. These and the social-revolutionists concluded and signed a mutual agreement as to their future cooperation.

Captain Wasilenko stated that there were found papers in the possession of a certain Mrs. Rocrich, which proved that the social-revolutionaries' plan was to destroy the army. (His further statements were heard within closed doors, the public not being admitted.)

Mr. Soloveitchik described the activity of Rogovsky. He was entrusted in Samara with the work of organizing the Police Ministry and accepted in the militia only social-revolutionaries who were known to the leaders of the party and who already had worked in terroristic organizations. He accepted also Bolsheviks. This militia naturally persecuted the army officers and the members of the Constitutional-Democratic parties

while the Bolsheviks could do anything which pleased them in Samara. When Rogovski was transferred to Omsk, he took with him the greater part of his militia, witness said.

Sentence of Expulsion.

After hearing of these witnesses the Military Court gave judgement as follows:—

The Court finds that some members of the central committee of the social revolutionary party and some other members of this party composed and spread a proclamation in which they appealed for the mobilization and arming of all members of the party with the purpose of overthrowing the All Russian Provisional Government, to re-establish a local Duma and to undermine the discipline in the army which is undesirable for the party.

"Rogovsky, together with other members of the social revolutionary party, organized an armed detachment with the object of removing from among the above-named party the members of the Directorate, General Boldyreff and Mr. Vologodsky, and for the purpose of terrorizing army officers and other persons. All of this being a criminal deed, the accused are to be handed over as guilty of criminal offence to the Minister of Justice for trial.

Subsequently it was decided to expel the four men from Russia after they had promised not to take any further part in Russian politics. They were guarded by their own request during the journey, being afraid of the infuriated people. General Knox kindly gave them some British soldiers to escort them out of Russia. They were not allowed to communicate with anybody during the whole journey and were set free only in Changchun.

《字林西报》。日期：18年12月11日。 2393/12/18

政变
鄂木斯克。

AVKSENTIEFF 及其
同伴在上海。

对他们的指控。

作者：George Synnerberg 上尉。

上周四，即12月5日，N. D. Avksentieff、Argunoff、Zenzinoff 和 Rogoffsky 先生抵达上海，他们是前俄国临时政府成员，也是11月18日在鄂木斯克被推翻的五人执政内阁成员。

这些俄国革命的使徒曾经拥有巨大的影响力，不仅在俄国，甚至在国外也广为人知，其中该党最杰出的人物 Avksentieff 先生，先后担任过俄国农民苏维埃主席、布尔什维克政变期间的内政部长、萨马拉和乌法的临时政府主席，以及后来的鄂木斯克俄国临时政府主席。在此职位上，他的职责是抵抗布尔什维克，并支持组建一支新的俄国军队，与英勇的捷克斯洛伐克军团以及英国、法国和意大利分遣队并肩作战，共同对抗叛徒和德国人。从下文中我们将看到这位先生是如何履行其职责的。由于他和他的同伴在鄂木斯克被捕，并在承诺不再参与俄国政治后被驱逐出俄国，且他们的意图是前往英国，或许英国公众会有兴趣了解他们被捕和驱逐的确切原因。

军事法庭证据。

这四位绅士于11月18日被几名哥萨克军官逮捕，这些军官随后接受了军事法庭审判，并在庭上提供了以下证词，译文摘自所有俄国报纸。

军官们并不否认逮捕了上述西伯利亚政府成员，但他们辩称无罪，因为迫使他们采取此类行动的唯一动机是他们拯救国家的强烈愿望。

Volkov 上校表示，他从一开始就看出新生的俄国政治家面临着非同寻常的困难。事态的发展使他确信，祖国的复兴任务受到了执政内阁某些成员的严重阻碍，即 Avksentieff、Argunoff、Zenzinoff 和 Rogoffsky 先生。后者从政治家的角度来看尤其完全不可接受。

前线的消息令人沮丧，据报道，由 V. Chernoc 领导的社会革命党正在进行极具破坏性的活动。

这种宣传开始在新生的西伯利亚军队队伍中引起不满。甚至在鄂木斯克本身，也组织了一支秘密的布尔什维克力量。

私人电报线路。

电报服务主管 Gleboff 上尉作证称，Avksentieff 与某位 Foganoffsky 之间通过直通线路与乌法政府进行了秘密谈话。Avksentieff 抱怨工作非常艰难，他不得不与一支“有纪律”的军队作斗争。

Gleboff 上尉说，Rogoffsky、Zenzinoff、Moiseenko 和 Brushvidt 也经常使用这条直通线路。记录纸带总是被销毁或带回家。Avksentieff 常带着自己的操作员来到电报局，并坚持不让普通操作员在场。电报主管收到消息，称有一名未知人士要求 Moiseenko 出于未知目的从国家资源中调拨1亿卢布。

总司令部军事情报局局长 Zlobin 上校陈述，他已获得有关社会革命党人企图推翻现政府的情报，他们秘密组建了一个中央委员会，据称成员包括 Avksentieff、Chernoff、Argunoff、Vedeniapine、Volsky、Handelman、Gourevitch、Brushwid、Minor、Rogowski、Klimushkine、Fortunatoff、Fenigovsky、Lazareff 和 Meistracht 等先生。该党的目标是推翻政府（该政府得到协约国的支持），证人表示他们甚至为此采取了一些步骤。他说，他们坚持要求将一支约200人、表现出布尔什维克同情倾向的分遣队从新尼古拉耶夫斯克（Novo-Nikolaevsk）调往鄂木斯克。在乌法，类似的布尔什维克分遣队在制宪会议成员 Fortunatoff 和 Klimouskin 的领导下组建。军事首长、社会革命党人 Kalinin 正向不同的军事单位派遣煽动者。Springowitch 少尉被任命为军事情报部门负责人，尽管已证实他具有非常明显的布尔什维克倾向。

布尔什维克部队与资金。

Affanasieff 上尉陈述：社会革命党人已为其未来内阁部长职位准备好了党派候选人，并且据悉 Avksentieff 掌握着约2亿卢布，证人断言这笔钱是布尔什维克部队寄给他在鄂木斯克的。这些人与社会革命党人签订并签署了一份关于未来合作的相互协议。

Wasilenko 上尉陈述，在某位 Rocrich 女士处发现了文件，证明社会革命党的计划是摧毁军队。（他的进一步陈述在不公开庭审中进行，公众不得旁听。）

Soloveitchik 先生描述了 Rogovsky 的活动。他在萨马拉受命组织警察部的工作，仅在民兵中接纳那些为党派领导人所知且已在恐怖组织中工作过的社会革命党人。他也接纳布尔什维克。这支民兵自然迫害军队军官和立宪民主党成员，

而布尔什维克在萨马拉可以为所欲为。证人称，当 Rogovski 被调往鄂木斯克时，他带走了大部分民兵。

驱逐判决。

在听取这些证人的证词后，军事法庭作出如下判决：—

法庭认定，社会革命党中央委员会的一些成员及该党其他成员起草并散布了一份宣言，呼吁动员并武装所有党员，目的是推翻全俄临时政府，重建地方杜马，并破坏军队纪律，因为军队纪律对该党不利。

“Rogovsky 与社会革命党的其他成员一起，组织了一支武装分遣队，目的是从上述政党中移除执政内阁成员、Boldyreff 将军和 Vologodsky 先生，并旨在恐吓军队军官及其他人员。鉴于所有这些均属犯罪行为，被告作为刑事罪犯移交给司法部长进行审判。”

随后，在这四人承诺不再进一步参与俄国政治后，决定将他们驱逐出俄国。应他们自己的请求，他们在旅途中受到护卫，因为他们害怕愤怒的民众。Knox 将军好心地提供了一些英国士兵护送他们离开俄国。在整个旅程中，他们不被允许与任何人联系，直到长春才被释放。

The Shanghai Gazette dated 11th. December, 1918

Mr. N. Avxentieff Writes to
"Vienna Tageblatt"

To the Editor, Shanghai Gazette.

Sir,—You were so kind as to publish in your paper my interview with Mr. "True to the End". I should like to give to your readers a brief explanation regarding the political events which occurred in Omsk.

Now in reference to my interview there appeared today in your paper an anonymous article signed "Vassily Dokounine" the author of which is Mr. Argunoff. Always "faithful unto the End". While this article contains no proofs in support of his assertions and contains nothing but insinuations and abuse of the Bolsheviks.

Indeed Mr. "True to the End" as we shall call him henceforth does remain true to the end to himself as well to others of his kin is hiding himself behind a pseudonym in order to pour out the basest calumnies and insinuations without having the courage to face openly full personal responsibility for his words. The true character of this author is given out by the last section of his letter: he does not understand the struggle for ideals and being "true to the end" he is eager to hurt me materially by insinuating the necessity of depriving me of hotel-accommodation during my temporary stay in Shanghai. But then he must substantially extend his good work. If we are ordinary "traitors" then my friend Kerensky is an arch-traitor, why then is Mr. "True to the End" not alarmed by the fact that the "arch-traitor" Kerensky is not only enjoying the hospitality of England but is being welcomed by official representatives of the government of that country as well as by representatives of other allied governments. Or perhaps those allied ministers who welcomed Kerensky are also traitors.

Mr. "True to the End" alleges that the Russian army was disorganised by the revolution and that the old tsarist regime was about to introduce reforms which, as he himself confesses, were indeed badly needed. This is false from the bottom. During two and a half years of his criminal policy the tsarist regime has brought about the complete disorganisation of the army which was systematically deprived of its most essential necessities and by treason delivered to the enemy. It is sufficient to recall that the principal wirepuller and inspirer of the tsarist regime was a man like the notorious Rasputin and his satellites in order to have a clear idea what sort of reforms the rotten to the root regime could introduce in the army and unfortunate country. Tsarism and its "True to the End" serviles brought finally the country to an abyss, for the recovery of which it is necessary superhuman efforts should be made; and the same abyss is now facing Germany owing to her Kaiserism and the serviles of this dying regime.

The Russian Revolution gave the Russian patriots some hope for the regeneration of the country, but alas the hope was not justified. At the moment when the revolution broke out this hope was cherished not only by the despised revolutionaries and democrats but practically by the whole country. That is why Tsarism was so easily done away with. Tsarism was opposed and the overthrow supported not only by socialists but also by such men as Miliukoff, Rodichev and other leaders of the constitutional-democratic party, also by the conservative Octobrists supported by such a man as Goutchkoff. All these parties joined in the struggle against Tsarism and helped the revolution.

But the hopes of the Russian people were soon shattered. The Provisional Government which came into power after the fall of Tsarism proved itself unable to cope with the difficult situation. It was composed of men who had no experience in governing and who were more interested in their own personal ambitions than in the welfare of the country. The result was chaos and anarchy. The Bolsheviks took advantage of this situation and seized power in October 1917. They established a dictatorship and began to persecute all those who opposed them. Many innocent people were arrested and executed. The country was plunged into a civil war which lasted for several years.

I am one of those who fought against the Bolsheviks from the very beginning. I was a member of the Union for the Regeneration of Russia which was formed in Siberia in August 1918. This organisation comprised all anti-Bolshevik parties and positively all popular governments. I was firstly elected as president of the conference and then as head of the new constituted All-Russian Government. It was I who offered to Kolchak who is a military expert the portfolio of the Ministry for military and naval affairs in my cabinet. He accepted my offer and I signed the mandate for his appointment. The same Kolchak with the aid of a group of reactionary officers conspired against me till he overthrew me, what brought about the dissolution of the government and the actual chaos.

I hope that these concise notes will give to you, Mr. Editor, as well as to the general public a clear idea of the value of utterances made by men like Mr. "True to the End". And if they are really true to the end then it is perhaps in sitting in Shanghai or in some other safe place to abuse, cast aspersions and shamelessly calumniate those who in a right or wrong way do not hesitate to put at stake their personal safety and their life for the general and be sure that they will not hesitate to do so in the future.

I am, etc.
N. AVXENTIEFF.

P. S. In a local morning paper to-day appeared about the events in Omsk an article which is full of misstatements in order to mislead the public. The facts are quoted from Russian papers which are inspired by partisans of the coup d'etat and are published under the strictest censorship. The best refutation of these statements are the actual events which have already taken place and which are known to everybody.

《上海公报》，1918年12月11日

N. 阿夫克森季耶夫先生致信
《维也纳日报》

致《上海公报》编辑：

先生，承蒙贵报刊登我与“始终如一”先生的访谈，不胜感激。我想就鄂木斯克发生的政治事件，向贵报读者作一简要说明。

关于我的访谈，今日贵报刊登了一篇署名为“瓦西里·多库宁”的匿名文章，其作者实为阿尔古诺夫先生。真可谓“始终如一”。虽然这篇文章没有任何证据支持其断言，除了对布尔什维克的暗示和谩骂之外，空无一物。

事实上，这位我们此后将称之为“始终如一”先生的作者，确实对自己以及他的同类“始终如一”，他躲在笔名后面，倾吐最卑鄙的诽谤和暗示，却没有勇气公开面对自己言论的全部个人责任。该作者的真实面目在其信的最后一部分暴露无遗：他不理解为理想而斗争的意义，并且为了“始终如一”，他急于通过暗示在我暂居上海期间剥夺我的旅馆住宿来在物质上伤害我。但他必须大大扩展他的“善行”。如果我们是普通的“叛徒”，那么我的朋友克伦斯基就是头号叛徒，那为何“始终如一”先生对“头号叛徒”克伦斯基不仅享受英国的款待，而且受到该国政府官方代表以及其他协约国政府代表的欢迎这一事实不感到惊慌呢？或者也许那些欢迎克伦斯基的协约国部长们也是叛徒。

“始终如一”先生声称，俄国军队被革命搞得混乱不堪，而旧的沙皇政权正准备引入改革，正如他自己承认的那样，这些改革确实是迫切需要的。这完全是彻头彻尾的谎言。在其犯罪政策的两年半期间，沙皇政权导致军队完全瓦解，系统性地剥夺了其最基本的必需品，并通过背叛将其交给敌人。只要回想一下，沙皇政权的主要幕后操纵者和鼓动者是像臭名昭著的拉斯普京及其党羽这样的人，就足以清楚地了解这个从根子上腐烂的政权能在军队和不幸的国家中引入什么样的改革。沙皇制度及其“始终如一”的奴才最终将国家推向了深渊，为了恢复国家，需要付出超人的努力；而由于德皇制度及其垂死政权的奴才，德国现在也面临着同样的深渊。

俄国革命给俄国爱国者带来了一些国家复兴的希望，但唉，这希望并未实现。在革命爆发的那一刻，这种希望不仅为受蔑视的革命者和民主派所珍视，实际上也为整个国家所珍视。这就是为什么沙皇制度如此容易被废除的原因。反对沙皇制度并支持推翻它的，不仅是社会主义者，还有米留可夫、罗季切夫以及立宪民主党的其他领导人，还有由古奇科夫这样的人支持的保守的十月党人。所有这些政党都加入了反对沙皇制度的斗争，并帮助了革命。

但是俄国人民的希望很快就破灭了。沙皇制度垮台后上台的临时政府证明无力应对困难局面。它由一些没有治理经验的人组成，他们更关心自己的个人野心，而不是国家的福祉。结果是混乱和无政府状态。布尔什维克利用了这一局势，于1917年10月夺取了政权。他们建立了独裁统治，并开始迫害所有反对他们的人。许多无辜的人被捕并被处决。国家陷入了一场持续数年的内战。

我是从一开始就与布尔什维克作战的人之一。我是1918年8月在西伯利亚成立的“俄国复兴联盟”的成员。该组织包括了所有反布尔什维克政党以及事实上所有的民众政府。我首先当选为会议主席，随后担任新组建的全俄政府的首脑。是我向作为军事专家的科尔恰克提供了我内阁中陆海军部长的职位。他接受了我的提议，我签署了他的任命状。正是同一个科尔恰克，在一群反动军官的帮助下阴谋反对我，直到他推翻了我，这导致了政府的解散和实际的混乱。

我希望这些简略的记录能使您，编辑先生，以及公众清楚地了解像“始终如一”先生这样的人的言论的价值。如果他们真的“始终如一”，那么也许就是坐在上海或其他安全的地方，辱骂、诋毁和厚颜无耻地诽谤那些无论对错都毫不犹豫地为大众利益拿个人安全和生命冒险的人，并且可以肯定，他们在未来也会毫不犹豫地这样做。

此致，
N. 阿夫克森季耶夫。

THE SHANGHAI GAZETTE, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 7. 1918
Avksentieff Tells of His Fight
for Democracy in Russia
People Looked to Him for Salvation from
Autocratic Rule—Just When Factions
Had Been Joined Comes Overthrow—
Charge of Bolshevist Sympathies Refuted

M. Nicolai Avksentieff

Mr. Niolai Avksentieff, famous head of the
Directoire of Five, the man who seemed
destined to re-unite All Russia on a truly
democratic basis, a man after the heart of
President Wilson, but deposed of power by
brutal force and a refugee in our town now,
gave a spirited interview to a reporter
of the Shanghai Gazette in the Kalee
Hotel to-day. His words will convince the
public that here was a chance for Russia,
and this chance was lost when the head of
the directoire fell before brute force of his
rivals leaving Russia again in danger of
being returned to aristocratic rule.
Mr. Avksentieff was an intimate of the
great Kerensky and worked with him to
abolish Tsarist power. Under the republic
he was Minister of Interior in the Kerensky
government and most of the beneficent new
laws are due to his untiring work for the
good of Russia.

《上海公报》，1918年12月7日，星期六
阿夫克森季耶夫讲述他在俄国为民主而战
人民指望他从专制统治中获得拯救——正当各派系联合之时却遭遇推翻——驳斥同情布尔什维克的指控

尼古拉·阿夫克森季耶夫先生

尼古拉·阿夫克森季耶夫先生，著名的“五人执政内阁”首领，这位似乎注定要在真正民主的基础上重新统一全俄国的人，这位深得威尔逊总统欢心的人，如今却被暴力剥夺权力并成为我们城市的难民，今天在华利饭店（Kalee Hotel）接受了《上海公报》记者的热情采访。他的话将使公众相信，俄国曾有过一个机会，而当执政内阁首脑在其对手的 brute force（暴力）面前倒下时，这个机会丧失了，使俄国再次面临回归贵族统治的危险。
阿夫克森季耶夫先生是伟大的克伦斯基的密友，并与他一起致力于废除沙皇权力。在共和国时期，他是克伦斯基政府的内政部长，大多数有益的新法律都归功于他为俄国福祉所做的不懈努力。

pages.en:
When the Bolshevik flood came he stood
maufully against the mad tide, fearless and
brave until all Russia was inundated. Then
he fled to France, the true home of sane
democracy, and worked unceasingly for
overthrow of the Bolsheviks. In conjunction
with his faithful collaborator Argonnoff,
he edited the paper L'Appel at Paris. Albert
Thomas the French minister of munitions,
Hyndman, the English socialist; Pablo
Eglesias and the Russian socialist Plesh-
kanoff were contributors.
Looked to Him for Aid
All the democratic elements in Russia
looked to him for salvation, and, therefore
Trotsky and his ilk called him traitor and
bourgeois. Finally with utter contempt for
danger he returned to Russia and was soon
at the head of a body of men styled the
Council of Provisional Government of the
Republic.
He soon had to flee from Petro-
grad, first to the army, and then
to Moscow, but in March 1918 he was
arrested and confined to the Peter-Paul
fortress where already were confined most
of the Kerensky cabinet members.
Just at this time the unhappy Singareff
and Kokoshkin were murdered, they were
sick, but brought from the hospital and
brutally slain. Mr. Avksentieff also was
condemned to death but managed to escape
to Siberia to continue his fight against the
Bolsheviks.
In Siberia he succeeded in uniting
all the parties, bourgeois and socia-
list, under the famous Directoire of Five and
Russia seemed on the way at last to return
to sanity. Then, alas for unhappy Russia,
there appeared Koltshak, the fierce and
vigorous Koltshak; a brave admiral perhaps
but an impossibility for democratic Russia.
The conference at Ufa had begun to bear
fruit; it was there that the so-called "sacred
union" was founded. It is true, the members
could at that time be elected only from and
by voters of Siberia, Samara, Turkestan
and Cossack territory, but it united all the
parties with the sole exception of the Bol-
shevics.
But the sinister Koltshak arrived at the
scene and with him came the icy wind of
dictatorship. Who was supporting Koltshak?
Only the military, Cossacks and old regime
officers but certainly not the population.
Tells of His Arrest
One night, it was the 18th of November,
the coup d'état came. "My house was
surrounded" said Mr. Avksentieff, "by a
party of 50 soldiers each carrying two
rifles. All were drunk and they arrested
us without producing any thing of authority
only the order came from Koltshak, the
dictator.
"Two days I and my followers were
imprisoned. On the third day Koltshak
demanded that we sign a paper renouncing
all authority and agreeing not to return to
Russia until a definite government had been
established.
"We flatly refused to do so. Finally we
were placed in a special train and conveyed
to the Chinese frontier. There was no pre-
tence of justice, it was brute force. We were
deported, well, that is not the worst.

当布尔什维克的洪水来袭时，他勇敢地对抗这股疯狂的潮流，无畏且勇敢，直到整个俄国被淹没。随后他逃往法国，那是健全民主的真正家园，并为推翻布尔什维克而不懈工作。与他忠实的合作者阿尔贡诺夫一起，他在巴黎编辑了《呼唤报》（L'Appel）。法国军需部长阿尔贝·托马斯、英国社会主义者海因德曼、巴勃罗·伊格莱西亚斯以及俄国社会主义者普列什卡诺夫都是撰稿人。
指望他援助
俄国所有的民主力量都指望他获得拯救，因此，托洛茨基及其同伙称他为叛徒和资产阶级。最后，他全然不顾危险，返回俄国，并很快成为被称为“共和国临时政府委员会”的一群人的首领。
他很快不得不逃离彼得格勒，先去了军队，然后去了莫斯科，但在1918年3月，他被捕并被关押在彼得保罗要塞，那里已经关押了大多数克伦斯基内阁成员。
就在此时，不幸的辛加列夫和科科什金被谋杀，他们当时生病，但被从医院带出并残忍杀害。阿夫克森季耶夫先生也被判处死刑，但设法逃往西伯利亚，继续他与布尔什维克的斗争。
在西伯利亚，他成功地在著名的“五人执政内阁”下联合了所有政党，包括资产阶级和社会主义者，俄国似乎终于走上了回归理智的道路。然而，唉，不幸的俄国，出现了科尔恰克，凶猛而精力充沛的科尔恰克；也许是一位勇敢的海军上将，但对于民主的俄国来说是不可能的。乌法会议开始结出果实；正是在那里，所谓的“神圣联盟”成立了。诚然，当时的成员只能由西伯利亚、萨马拉、突厥斯坦和哥萨克地区的选民选举产生并由其选出，但它联合了除布尔什维克以外的所有政党。
但是阴险的科尔恰克来到了现场，随之而来的是独裁的寒风。谁在支持科尔恰克？只有军人、哥萨克和旧政权军官，但肯定不是民众。
讲述他的逮捕
一天夜里，即11月18日，政变发生了。“我的房子被包围了，”阿夫克森季耶夫先生说，“由50名士兵组成的一队人，每人携带两支步枪。他们都喝醉了，在没有出示任何授权文件的情况下逮捕了我们，命令仅来自独裁者科尔恰克。
“我和我的追随者被监禁了两天。第三天，科尔恰克要求我们签署一份文件，放弃所有权力，并同意在确定政府成立之前不返回俄国。
“我们断然拒绝这样做。最后，我们被置于一列专车上，被运往中国边境。没有假装公正，这是赤裸裸的暴力。我们被驱逐出境，好吧，这还不是最糟糕的。

"Nothing can be more ridiculous. I was
condemned to death by those very Bolsh-

who also was condemned to death, in fact
every one of my followers; here is Mr.

And what will be Kolchak's policy? "I
fear that he may cause Russia again to
split into the parties so hardly united. At
present there is no such indication as the
parties seem to accept him as one who
might be necessary at the present moment
since he is a man who may command the
new Russian army of 300,000 men."
Asked about his intentions Mr. Avksen-
tieff said that he was going to London and
Paris and eventually, when Russia is
liberated, to return there. He thinks
that Prince Lvoff might be chosen to
represent Russia on the Peace conference
table, and said: "I might also be there."
Here one of his followers remarked:
"Kolchak's calumnies are even influenc-
ing people here. There are dark undercur-
rents and they might put obstacles into our
way." Mr. Avksentieff remarked that
when he was in power he gave a passport
to Mr. Zevinkoff who departed for Europe
via Shanghai where the Russian Consul duly
honored the document. "Now I, who issued
that paper, might not have the same facility."

甚至进一步指责我们 favoring the Bolshevics（偏向布尔什维克），声称与他们进行了秘密谈判，并且由于科尔恰克实施了严格的审查制度，他能够对外界造成这种影响。
他甚至诱使路透社代理人发电报称，我们因倾向布尔什维克而被罢免。
并不喜爱布尔什维克
“没有什么比这更荒谬的了。我正是被那些布尔什维克判处死刑，在彼得保罗要塞受苦，这里是我的同事阿尔古诺夫先生，他也被判处死刑，事实上，我的每一个追随者都是如此；这里是津济诺夫先生，他甚至被判处过两次死刑，”他微笑着说，“而科尔恰克，嗯，他在东京或上海很安全。”
科尔恰克的政策将会是什么？“我担心他可能会导致俄国再次分裂成那些难以联合的派系。目前还没有这样的迹象，因为各派系似乎接受他，认为他在当前时刻可能是必要的，因为他是一个可能指挥30万人的新俄国军队的人。”
当被问及他的意图时，阿夫克森季耶夫先生说，他打算去伦敦和巴黎，并最终在俄国获得解放时返回那里。他认为李沃夫亲王可能会被选为代表俄国出席和平会议的人选，并说：“我也可能会在那里。”
这时，他的一位追随者评论道：“科尔恰克的诽谤甚至影响了这里的人们。存在暗流，他们可能会给我们的道路设置障碍。”阿夫克森季耶夫先生 remarked that（指出），当他掌权时，他给泽温科夫先生签发了一本护照，后者经上海前往欧洲，那里的俄国领事 duly honored the document（正式认可了该文件）。“现在，我这个签发该文件的人，可能就没有同样的便利了。”

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
NOVEMBER 26. 1918.
THE COUP D'ETAT
AT OMSK.

OLD ORDER ACCUSED OF
BOLSHEVISM.

COSSACK ACTION.

Through Reuter's Agency.

Harbin, Nov. 24.
The following is an official report
concerning the coup d'état at Omsk
on the night of November 18:—
"Owing to indisputable proofs that
Avksentieff, Zenzinoff, Argunoff and
Rogovski were negotiating with the
Bolsheviks and had organized a
criminal propaganda in the young
Russian army, the majority of the
populace of Omsk and sound poli-
tical parties frequently but un-
successfully tried to draw the atten-
tion of the high authorities to the
situation, warning them of its dis-
astrous results. Finally they decid-
ed to act on their own responsibility
and to arrest the above four mem-
bers of the Directoire, using for
this purpose the regiments of the
Omsk garrison, which were especial-
ly discontented.
"The plan was carried out on the
night of November 18. The arrest-
ed Ministers were not harmed and
were kept in a house of the Agricul-
tural School. The following morn-
ing three Cossack officers in com-
mand of the regiments presented
themselves at Admiral Koltchak's
headquarters and declared that the
arrest was carried out by their
orders. Well knowing, and acknow-
ledging, that they had committed a
crime by acting without orders
of the authorities, the officers them-
selves requested the Admiral to
order them to be tried according to
martial law, being ready to sacrifice
their lives for the sake of Russia.
This order was immediately given.
"The arrested Ministers were
freed, but well knowing the hostility
of the population towards them,
they preferred to remain under
guard. At the same time they ap-
pealed to the Government, begging
permission to leave Russia and pro-
mising never again to take a part
in Russian politics. The officers
were found not guilty and were re-
leased. The fate of the Ministers is
not yet known. Communications
in Siberia have been everywhere
restored and complete order pre-
vails, all authorities acting in full
accord. All sound elements of the
population and army are looking to
the future with entire confidence."
General Horvath has appealed to
the population of Far Eastern
Siberia, announcing the names of
the new Government, forbidding the
holding of public meetings in the
open air or in private houses with-
out special permission and warning
that any attempt at propaganda
against the Government will be
dealt with according to martial law.
Harbin, Nov. 25.
A Reuter's correspondent is officially
informed that the former Ministers
of the Siberian Government,
Avksentieff, Argunoff, Zenzinoff and
Rogovski have left Omsk for Chang-
chun.

《字林西报》，
1918年11月26日。
鄂木斯克政变。

旧秩序被指控为布尔什维克主义。

哥萨克人的行动。

据路透社电。

哈尔滨，11月24日。
以下是关于11月18日夜鄂木斯克政变的官方报告：——
“由于有确凿证据表明阿夫克森季耶夫（Avksentieff）、津济诺夫（Zenzinoff）、阿尔古诺夫（Argunoff）和罗戈夫斯基（Rogovski）正在与布尔什维克谈判，并在年轻的俄罗斯军队中组织了犯罪宣传，鄂木斯克的大多数民众以及稳健的政党虽频繁但未能成功地提请高层当局注意局势，警告其灾难性后果。最终，他们决定自行承担责任，利用特别不满的鄂木斯克驻军团逮捕了上述四位执政内阁成员。
“该计划于11月18日夜执行。被捕部长未受伤害，被关押在农业学校的一所房屋内。次日清晨，指挥各团的三名哥萨克军官前往科尔恰克海军上将（Admiral Koltchak）总部，声明逮捕行动是奉他们的命令执行的。这些军官深知并承认，他们在未经当局命令的情况下采取行动已构成犯罪，因此主动请求海军上将下令按军法审判他们，表示愿为俄罗斯牺牲生命。该命令随即下达。
“被捕部长获释，但因深知民众对他们的敌意，他们宁愿继续处于监护之下。同时，他们向政府呼吁，恳请允许离开俄罗斯，并承诺不再参与俄罗斯政治。军官们被判无罪并获释。部长们的命运尚不清楚。西伯利亚各地的通讯均已恢复，秩序井然，所有当局行动完全一致。民众和军队中的所有稳健分子都对未来充满信心。”
霍尔瓦特将军（General Horvath）已向西伯利亚远东地区的民众发出呼吁，公布新政府成员名单，禁止在未经许可的情况下在户外或私人住宅举行公共集会，并警告任何针对政府的宣传企图都将按军法处置。
哈尔滨，11月25日。
路透社记者正式获悉，前西伯利亚政府部长阿夫克森季耶夫（Avksentieff）、阿尔古诺夫（Argunoff）、津济诺夫（Zenzinoff）和罗戈夫斯基（Rogovski）已离开鄂木斯克前往长春。

（右上角手写批注：2393 7·12·19.）
